destination.title: De Sitter existence, scalar instability and candidate exceptions
destination.question: Which mechanisms and consistency conditions restrict de Sitter existence and scalar stability, and how do proposed exceptions and related conjectural arguments test those restrictions?
destination.summary: A navigational family with distinct questions about statistical rarity, structural tachyons, no-scale deformations, necessary existence conditions and candidate consistency. Its numerical membership does not establish a common theorem, physical regime or fine question identity.

systems: Classical type IIA and type IIB compactification searches
General no-scale F-term supergravity as an overlapping setting
Scalar quantum-breaking arguments as comparative alternate scope

Conditional comparison with de Sitter conjectures
regimes: Small deformations near no-scale Minkowski vacua

assumptions: Every obstruction and candidate retains its own hypotheses
Conjectures under examination are not accepted family premises

conventions: Selected scalar-sector stability is distinguished from full physical-spectrum stability
Reported flat directions are distinguished from strictly positive masses

evidence.text: How unlikely is a tachyon-free de Sitter extremum in classical Type IIA searches, and does raising vacuum energy destabilize initially positive-mass configurations through increased moduli mixing?

sources.title: Tachyons in Classical de Sitter Vacua

evidence.text: What explains the recurring tachyons in two classical type II de Sitter constructions, why do they generally miss the sgoldstino direction, and what conditional guidance follows for searches for metastability?

sources.title: Further refining the de Sitter swampland conjecture

evidence.text: Could additional classical ingredients yield non-tachyonic positive vacua and challenge refined de Sitter conjectures? The paper identifies candidates while emphasizing that their microscopic consistency remains unresolved.

sources.title: On stable type IIA de-Sitter vacua with geometric flux

evidence.text: Can a geometric type IIA orientifold evade known de Sitter no-go conditions and yield tachyon-free extrema with integral fluxes, while maintaining useful moduli control and satisfying the available Bianchi identities?

sources.title: A Global View on The Search for de-Sitter Vacua in (type IIA) String Theory

evidence.text: Numerically count positive-definite real symmetric random matrices. Compare complete GOE matrices with M=A+B, where positive diagonal A represents an initially stabilized configuration and random B models additional mixing. Fit probabilities with P=a exp(−bN²−cN).

sources.title: Tachyons in Classical de Sitter Vacua

evidence.text: Dimensionally reduce to four-dimensional Einstein frame, retaining dilaton and selected metric rescalings; match the resulting potentials to F-term potentials obtained from stated Kähler potentials and superpotentials.

sources.title: Further refining the de Sitter swampland conjecture

evidence.text: Bound the gradient power below and curvature above, combine them with positive a, and cancel n′/n. In this paper the cancellation works algebraically, but its curvature input does not follow from the stated assumptions as presently rendered.

sources.title: On stable type IIA de-Sitter vacua with geometric flux

evidence.text: Decompose the scalar potential into RR, NS–NS/geometric, and local/tadpole pieces with explicit volume, complex-structure, and dilaton dependence. First apply volume–dilaton extremization and Hessian conditions, then include the remaining moduli; passing the two-field test is only necessary.

sources.title: A Global View on The Search for de-Sitter Vacua in (type IIA) String Theory

evidence.text: Compute concrete moduli mass matrices from K and W, transform to canonical kinetic variables, and examine principal submatrices. In the universal volume/dilaton sector, use flux/source scaling laws, extremum equations and determinant/trace positivity to diagnose stability.

sources.title: Tachyons in Classical de Sitter Vacua

evidence.text: Solve the IIA ten-dimensional equations perturbatively in the small parameter defined by a³/v²; compare truncated analytic expansions with numerical solutions. No all-order analytic solution is obtained.

sources.title: A Universal Tachyon in Nearly No-scale de Sitter Compactifications

evidence.text: Which structural conditions force a tachyon in de Sitter solutions obtained by small deformations of no-scale Minkowski vacua, and which ingredients can evade this obstruction?

sources.title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions

evidence.text: Does the selected scalar sector reveal a tachyon in every classical de Sitter solution with intersecting sources?

sources.title: New constraints on classical de Sitter: flirting with the swampland

evidence.text: Can classical type II compactifications with parallel orientifold and D-brane sources support de Sitter spacetime? If solutions exist, do volume, dilaton, and source-adapted anisotropy fluctuations necessarily contain a tachyon?

sources.title: A note on obstinate tachyons in classical dS solutions

evidence.text: Do the persistent tachyons in classical geometric de Sitter compactifications have a structural explanation in volume, dilaton and orientifold-cycle fluctuations, and how does this explanation connect to the sgoldstino near a supersymmetric limit?

sources.title: A new light on the darkest corner of the landscape

evidence.text: How sharp is the refined de Sitter constraint in massive IIA effective supergravities, and can a positive stationary point evade both its gradient and tachyonic-Hessian alternatives?

sources.title: On classical de Sitter solutions in higher dimensions

evidence.text: Which classical type-II orientifold compactifications to D>4 can satisfy necessary existence and perturbative-stability conditions for de Sitter vacua, as tested by the universal volume and dilaton directions?

destination.title: Dark-energy evolution, phantom interpretations and consistency
destination.question: What can departures from, or observational degeneracies with, w=-1 reveal about dark-energy dynamics, inference and theoretical viability?
destination.summary: A proposed family connecting observational discrimination with physical phantom dynamics, effective phantom interpretations, constrained scalar evolution and background lifetime. Cross-era connections and alternate questions remain separately accessible.

systems: Cosmological dark-energy fluids and scalar fields
targets: Perturbative stability, energy conditions and energy boundedness
Consistency and lifetime of evolving dark energy
regimes: Source-specific constant and evolving equations of state
Source-dated observations and conditional observational prospects
assumptions: Swampland restrictions are conditional frameworks in selected questions, not family-wide premises
Numerical selection roles do not determine scientific membership

sources.title: Quintom Cosmology: Theoretical implications and observations

evidence.text: How can dark energy cross w=−1 while maintaining acceptable background and perturbation dynamics, what observational signatures distinguish such quintom models, and how can their NEC-violating phases support bouncing or cyclic cosmologies?

sources.title: Implications of single field inflation in general cosmological scenarios on the nature of dark energy given the swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Could percent-level constraints on the dark-energy equation of state distinguish a modified-cosmology quintessence model from w=-1? The paper names several surveys and instruments as motivation for exploring that possibility.

sources.title: Cosmic birefringence from monodromic axion dark energy

evidence.text: Could periodic instanton corrections to monodromic dark energy leave observable oscillations while the field continues rolling monotonically?

sources.title: Reconstructing the dark energy equation of state with varying alpha

evidence.text: What information about the dark-energy equation of state w(z) can varying-α observations recover when the scalar–electromagnetic coupling is specified, and what measurement precision would be required?

sources.title: A Phantom menace?

evidence.text: Can a positive-density dark component with w < −1 produce a workable classical cosmology and satisfy the observational tests considered in the paper, and how would its background and perturbations differ from conventional dark energy?

sources.title: Quintom Cosmology: Theoretical implications and observations

evidence.text: The perturbation treatment combines field and metric fluctuations in conformal Newtonian gauge, separates adiabatic and isocurvature modes, and uses modified CAMB calculations to examine CMB and matter power spectra.

sources.title: Implications of single field inflation in general cosmological scenarios on the nature of dark energy given the swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Substitute the friction-dominated velocity into the canonical equation of state, use potential domination to eliminate V in favor of F, and transfer the slope inequality through a monotone rational function.

sources.title: Cosmic birefringence from monodromic axion dark energy

evidence.text: Evolve a specified potential from a frozen initial field, select the initial value to reproduce the present abundance, and translate the resulting displacement into a coupling. The principal application fixes the axion to all dark energy.

sources.title: Reconstructing the dark energy equation of state with varying alpha

evidence.text: Generate Gaussian simulated α data at z = 0.2–4 in steps of 0.2, with coupling chosen for variations around 10^(-5). Fit g(N) by polynomials, generally cubic and fifth order for the oscillating example.

sources.title: A Phantom menace?

evidence.text: Modify CMBfast for phantom perturbations using both scalar and generalized kinetic descriptions. Approximate the subhorizon mass-spectrum shape with BBKS and compare CMB normalization against a cluster-abundance extension to w < −1.

sources.title: Quintom Cosmology: Theoretical implications and observations

evidence.text: The no-go discussion analyzes gauge-invariant pressure, density and entropy perturbations, then scalar dispersion relations with c_s²=P_,X/ρ_,X. Negative sound-speed squared or a divergent dispersion relation supplies the stated obstruction to stable crossing.

sources.title: The Dynamics of Quintessence, The Quintessence of Dynamics

evidence.text: What must an experiment measure beyond a nearly cosmological-constant average equation of state?

sources.title: Uplifting, Depressing, and Tilting Dark Energy

evidence.text: Can single-field dark energy interactions produce the stronger mid-redshift and weaker recent acceleration indicated by the paper's distance-data interpretation, including crossing w=-1, while avoiding unacceptable changes to matter and structure growth?

sources.title: The Effective Theory of Quintessence: the w<-1 Side Unveiled

evidence.text: Can single-field dark energy have w_Q < -1 or cross w_Q = -1 without ghosts or dangerous gradient instabilities, and what perturbation phenomenology follows on cosmological scales?

sources.title: Hidden Negative Energies in Strongly Accelerated Universes

evidence.text: Can cosmological dark energy with healthy linear perturbations nevertheless admit arbitrarily negative observer-measured energies, and can imperfect stresses violate the null energy condition even when the measured equation of state satisfies w>−1?

sources.title: Runaway Quintessence, Out of the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a string modulus temporarily held near an unstable positive-energy maximum explain dark energy? The proposed mechanism must accommodate an equation of state near minus one, a tiny energy density, visible-sector constraints, and the eventual instability.

sources.title: Comments on the Transplanckian Censorship Conjecture

evidence.text: Does a rolling dark-energy configuration decay before initially Planck-scale fluctuations grow beyond the Hubble scale? The relevant transition is from a time-dependent scalar background to an isolated lower-energy state, rather than decay from a stationary false vacuum.

sources.title: The viability of phantom dark energy: A review

evidence.text: Can dark energy with w<−1 have a theoretically viable microscopic field description, or can ordinary fields and modified cosmological inference produce an apparent phantom equation of state without fundamental phantom dynamics?

sources.title: Bounds on Slow Roll and the de Sitter Swampland

evidence.text: How can a universal order-one slow-roll restriction coexist with dark energy whose measured equation of state is close to −1? The source presents this as a challenge for quintessence and de Sitter denial, while allowing evolving dark energy.

sources.title: Gradient instability for w < -1

evidence.text: In positive-density, single-scalar dark-energy models with w < -1, must fluctuations about a homogeneous background have negative gradient energy, and does this determine the time-kinetic sign?

sources.title: No-Go Theorem for Phantom Crossing in Scalar-Tensor Gravity with Non-Minimal Derivative Coupling and Soft Scale-Invariance Breaking

evidence.text: Can a single-scalar theory with non-minimal derivative coupling (NMDC) and softly broken scale invariance realize phantom behavior while satisfying perturbative stability and swampland conjectures? Motivation is the paper's historical account of the DESI 2024 preference, conditional on future confirmation.

sources.title: Multi-field dark energy: Cosmic acceleration on a steep potential

evidence.text: Can dark energy remain dynamically active on a steep potential while its equation of state resembles a cosmological constant? The paper investigates whether turning in field space permits this behavior and whether fluctuations can distinguish it observationally.

sources.title: Constraints on Dark Energy from Inflation and the Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: Can inflationary constraints on quantum-gravity conjecture parameters determine whether rolling dark energy must produce an observable departure from w=-1? The proposed connection uses a common EFT parameter and allows the inflaton and quintessence to be different fields.

sources.title: Isocurvature Perturbations of Dark Energy and Dark Matter from the Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a common lower bound on inflationary and quintessence potential gradients connect primordial quantum fluctuations, present dark energy, and interacting dark matter?

sources.title: The state of the dark energy equation of state circa 2023

evidence.text: Do cosmological datasets support a constant dark-energy equation of state different from −1, particularly slightly phantom values near −1.03, and what drives Planck-only phantom preferences?

sources.title: DESI results: hint towards coupled dark matter and dark energy

evidence.text: Can dark matter coupled to canonical quintessence produce an inferred dark-energy equation of state that crosses from below −1 in the past to above −1 today, while the scalar itself remains non-phantom and accommodates the DESI reconstruction?

sources.title: Null Energy Condition and Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: Can dark energy have w_de < −1 or cross −1 while the total cosmological stress tensor satisfies the null energy condition, and which Quintom examples realize this?

sources.title: From Swampland to Phenomenology and Back

evidence.text: Does dark energy evolve measurably rather than behave as a cosmological constant? The proposed test measures w(z)=p(z)/ρ(z) and compares it with −1, independently of whether swampland conjectures are correct.

sources.title: Can the dark energy equation-of-state parameter $w$ be less than $−1$?

evidence.text: Can negative-kinetic-energy scalar models realize dark energy with w<−1 while avoiding catastrophic decay over a cosmological lifetime, particularly when regarded as effective theories with a momentum cutoff?

sources.title: Testing for w< -1 in the solar system

evidence.text: Under what solar-system, pulsar-timing and gravitational-constant-variation constraints can scalar-tensor gravity yield an effective present dark-energy equation of state significantly below −1? Conversely, how could a robust measurement of w0 constrain departures from GR?

destination.title: Ultraviolet gravity, matter constraints and infrared tests
destination.question: Which gravity and gravity–matter theories admit controlled ultraviolet behavior, and how do their frameworks, approximations and infrared matching affect consistency and phenomenology?
destination.summary: Fixed-point calculations, matter constraints and observable construction form a coherent core. Cosmology, black holes and framework-relative swampland questions provide applications and comparisons. String worldsheets, cyclic holographic flows, extremal-functional spectra and many-species limits retain alternative homes without acquiring an asymptotic-safety premise.

targets: Dependence of consistency criteria on the ultraviolet framework
regimes: Candidate ultraviolet fixed points and connecting trajectories
Separate worldsheet, cyclic-flow and many-species limits
assumptions: Each source retains its own field content, truncation, symmetry and matching assumptions.
A fixed-point candidate is evidence within its approximation, not certification of a complete quantum theory.
Swampland criteria remain conjectured or framework-specific unless the supplied evidence establishes more.
conventions: Dimensions, coupling normalizations and background choices are source-specific.
Photon duality-frame conventions are not transferred to gauge-coupling calculations in other settings.
includes: Explicit alternate homes for questions outside the narrower asymptotic-safety core
excludes: Treating numerical membership as scientific equivalence
Inferring universal restrictions from one completion or truncation
Treating announced observational targets as established fits
Inferring a complete amplitude from numerical spectral zeros

sources.title: Curvature dependence of quantum gravity

evidence.text: Can curvature-dependent graviton fluctuation couplings support an asymptotically safe UV fixed point, and what backgrounds solve the background and quantum equations of motion, with and without Standard Model matter?

sources.title: A link that matters: Towards phenomenological tests of unimodular asymptotic safety

evidence.text: Can demanding ultraviolet-complete gauge and Yukawa sectors constrain unimodular asymptotic safety, standard asymptotically safe gravity, and Weyl-squared gravity? Are the leading Weyl-squared gravitational contributions universal within the functional RG calculation?

sources.title: Quantum Gravity: A Fluctuating Point of View

evidence.text: What evidence supports asymptotically safe quantum gravity when dynamical metric fluctuations are distinguished from the background, and how are background independence, locality, matter stability and unitarity addressed?

sources.title: Constraints on discrete global symmetries in quantum gravity

evidence.text: Can global Z_n interactions exist at an asymptotically safe gravity–matter fixed point, emerge as relevant deformations of a U(1)-symmetric fixed point, or generate large scalar mass hierarchies?

sources.title: The weak-gravity bound and the need for spin in asymptotically safe matter-gravity models

evidence.text: Can gravity coupled only to scalar fields admit an asymptotically safe fixed point once unavoidable derivative interactions are included, and can adding fermions or vectors restore viable fixed-point candidates?

sources.title: Lorentzian Quantum Gravity and the Graviton Spectral Function

evidence.text: Can a direct Lorentzian functional renormalisation group calculation produce an asymptotically safe gravitational fixed point and a graviton spectral function, providing timelike propagators needed for future scattering and unitarity tests?

sources.title: Status update: Asymptotically safe gravity-matter systems

evidence.text: What evidence, phenomenological predictions, consistency constraints, and unresolved problems characterize asymptotically safe gravity–matter systems, particularly Standard Model and beyond-Standard-Model sectors, as reviewed in January 2022?

sources.title: Form Factors in Asymptotically Safe Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: How can momentum-dependent form factors in the quantum effective action encode asymptotically safe gravitational observables, connect first-principles calculations to scattering amplitudes, and expose low-energy consistency conditions?

sources.title: Asymptotic safety of gravity with matter

evidence.text: Which matter content and interactions admit an asymptotically safe gravity–matter theory, and can ultraviolet quantum scale symmetry yield testable relations among low-energy Standard Model and beyond-Standard-Model parameters?

sources.title: Shift-symmetric Horndeski gravity in the asymptotic-safety paradigm

evidence.text: Can shift-symmetric kinetic-braiding Horndeski models admit an asymptotically safe quantum-field-theoretic UV completion, and can the resulting coupling constraints remain compatible with dynamical dark energy? A second analysis asks whether a gravitational EFT can yield viable couplings without new strongly coupled subplanckian physics.

sources.title: Towards theory constraints on ultralight dark matter from quantum gravity

evidence.text: Does asymptotically safe gravity permit a dimension-five scalar ULDM–gauge interaction, and can perturbative gravitational fluctuations generate or enhance that interaction? Projected nuclear-clock sensitivity motivates studying these questions at Planck-suppressed coupling strengths.

sources.title: Cosmology from asymptotically safe Proca theories

evidence.text: Which cosmologically motivated vector–tensor EFTs admit an asymptotically safe quantum-field-theory completion, and how could their UV critical surfaces restrict the infrared parameters relevant to late-time cosmology?

sources.title: Scalar-scalar-graviton vertex from Asymptotic Safety

evidence.text: What is the full momentum dependence of the scalar-scalar-graviton vertex within an analytically tractable asymptotic-safety approximation, and does its on-shell limit reproduce gravitational soft divergences? The vertex is an ingredient toward testing unitarity and causality through scattering amplitudes.

sources.title: An asymptotically safe guide to quantum gravity and matter

evidence.text: Review how interacting renormalization-group fixed points can provide predictive ultraviolet completions for matter and gravity, and whether gravity–matter interactions could connect Planck-scale dynamics to observable particle physics.

sources.title: Quantum Gravity from Dynamical Metric Fluctuations

evidence.text: Can metric quantum gravity possess an interacting UV fixed point with finitely many relevant directions, connect to general relativity and the Standard Model, and admit acceptable Lorentzian spectral properties? This contribution reviews the fluctuation-based functional RG evidence.

sources.title: Curvature dependence of quantum gravity

evidence.text: Approximate curved momentum space: symmetrise covariant derivatives, retain generated curvature terms, and replace derivative contractions by spectral magnitudes and flat-space angles. Angular integration factorises from spectral summation. The construction has the correct flat limit and is exact for terms containing only Laplacians.

sources.title: An asymptotically safe guide to quantum gravity and matter

evidence.text: Use perturbative loop and epsilon expansions for matter examples, and the Wetterich functional RG equation for gravity. Practical gravity calculations truncate curvature operators or fluctuation vertices; bimetric formulations and shift Ward identities address background dependence.

sources.title: A link that matters: Towards phenomenological tests of unimodular asymptotic safety

evidence.text: Test leading-order universality using regulator threshold integrals, linear and exponential metric parameterizations, and an interpolating parameterization. Individual diagram dependence is combined at the level of matter beta functions.

sources.title: Quantum Gravity: A Fluctuating Point of View

evidence.text: Flat-background Fourier expansions resolve tensor structures and momentum-dependent vertex dressings; heat-kernel or spectral methods project curvature invariants. The review argues that complete flat and curvature projections yield the same invariant coefficients, while incomplete operator bases introduce ambiguities.

sources.title: Constraints on discrete global symmetries in quantum gravity

evidence.text: Functional renormalization group for the scale-dependent effective action Γ_k, with an infrared regulator and projection onto truncated operator sets to obtain beta functions. Fixed points and relevant directions are assessed through beta-function zeros and stability-matrix eigenvalues.

sources.title: The weak-gravity bound and the need for spin in asymptotically safe matter-gravity models

evidence.text: Gravitational fixed-point locations are taken from existing beta functions in background and fluctuation approximations. In the latter, effective universality is assumed to identify the Newton-coupling avatars with the three-graviton avatar.

sources.title: Asymptotic safety, string theory and the weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Can string theory generate an effective gravity–matter theory with a long intermediate asymptotically safe regime, and what necessary scale-matching and weak-gravity conditions would such a scenario satisfy?

sources.title: Black Holes in Asymptotically Safe Gravity

evidence.text: What do asymptotic-safety-inspired models and effective-action/path-integral calculations imply for black-hole singularities, formation, evaporation and entropy, and which conclusions survive improvements to RG model building?

sources.title: On avoiding Ostrogradski instabilities within Asymptotic Safety

evidence.text: Can asymptotically safe gravity coupled to scalars accommodate dynamically generated higher-derivative scalar kinetic terms while admitting complete RG trajectories with ghost-free renormalized scalar propagators?

sources.title: Critical reflections on asymptotically safe gravity

evidence.text: What supports asymptotically safe gravity, which conceptual and technical obstacles remain, and how can fixed-point studies progress toward controlled calculations of observables?

sources.title: Scales and hierachies in asymptotically safe quantum gravity: a review

evidence.text: How can asymptotically safe gravity accommodate the observed cosmological constant and its hierarchy with the Planck scale, retain predictive power, and determine remaining gravitational couplings from cosmology?

sources.title: Troubles with global monopoles in quantum gravity

evidence.text: Can infrared gravitational properties of global monopoles obstruct spontaneously broken global symmetries through negative-energy pair production, assuming the Equivalence Principle and unbroken local Poincaré symmetry in the ultraviolet?

sources.title: Asymptotically safe cosmology – A status report

evidence.text: How can gravitational asymptotic safety connect ultraviolet fixed-point behavior to classical cosmology, inflation, primordial fluctuations and the initial singularity, and how far can resulting effective models be confronted with observations?

sources.title: Asymptotic safety in generalized Proca theories

evidence.text: Do generalized Proca theories admit a suitable interacting UV fixed point within quantum field theory, and does its behavior under enlarging the truncation support a predictive asymptotically safe completion?

sources.title: Cosmological α′-corrections from the functional renormalization group

evidence.text: Can T-duality constraints and functional renormalization group methods determine cosmological α′ corrections to all orders, with a suitable ultraviolet fixed point and an Einstein-like infrared limit?

sources.title: Hyperbolic field space and swampland conjecture for DBI scalar

evidence.text: Which scalar theories coupled to gravity admit a consistent UV completion? The reviewed refined de Sitter conjecture constrains the potential gradient or its most negative orthonormal covariant-Hessian eigenvalue for fields with a kinetic metric.

sources.title: QED coupled to QEG

evidence.text: Can QED coupled to asymptotically safe Quantum Einstein Gravity possess an interacting continuum limit, avoid its Landau singularity, and predict the infrared electric charge rather than require it as an independent input?

sources.title: The Weak Gravity Conjecture in Asymptotically Safe Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Can running gravitational and electromagnetic couplings in asymptotically safe quantum gravity modify charged-black-hole extremality so that the Weak Gravity Conjecture emerges from ultraviolet renormalization-group behavior?

sources.title: Approximate Symmetries and Gravity

evidence.text: Can a symmetry-protected high-dimensional operator generate an arbitrarily small Yukawa coupling without conflicting with gravitational restrictions on approximate global symmetries?

sources.title: Theta-problem and the String Swampland

evidence.text: Can a quantum-gravity completion permit continuously adjustable couplings that are independent of scalar expectation values?

evidence.text: Which matter spectra admit a viable asymptotically safe gravitational fixed point within the studied truncations, and could particle searches provide consistency tests of this quantum-gravity scenario?

sources.title: Constraining power of asymptotic safety for scalar fields

evidence.text: Can asymptotically safe gravity restrict interactions between a visible scalar sector and a scalar or Yukawa dark sector?

sources.title: Theta-problem and the String Swampland

evidence.text: Which gauge couplings and theta angles of an infrared photon coupled to gravity admit a consistent ultraviolet completion?

sources.title: Are there ALPs in the asymptotically safe landscape?

sources.title: Safe essential scalar-tensor theories

evidence.text: Within a complete four-derivative approximation for gravity coupled to a shift-symmetric scalar, do essential couplings admit an asymptotically safe UV completion connected to ordinary IR effective field theory, and what restrictions follow for scalar self-interactions?

sources.title: Viability of quantum-gravity induced ultraviolet completions for matter

evidence.text: Can the existence of interacting matter with viable electroweak properties constrain microscopic asymptotically safe gravity through real matter fixed points and RG trajectories accommodating finite fermion masses?

sources.title: The absolute swampland

evidence.text: Are swampland constraints universal across quantum-gravity completions or dependent on the UV framework? This review compares no-global-symmetries, weak-gravity and de-Sitter conjectures in string theory and asymptotic safety.

sources.title: Scalar-tensor theories within Asymptotic Safety

evidence.text: Can gravity coupled to one real scalar admit an asymptotically safe ultraviolet completion once mutually interacting, shift-symmetric scalar self-interactions and non-minimal curvature couplings are retained?

sources.title: Implications of the weak gravity conjecture in anomalous quiver gauge theories

evidence.text: Does a fixed ultraviolet completion realize the assumed light scalars and massless vectors, remove forbidden global symmetries, and satisfy stronger scalar criteria after potentials and corrections are included?

sources.title: The unitary conformal field theory behind 2D Asymptotic Safety

evidence.text: Can the Einstein–Hilbert truncation underlying Asymptotic Safety yield an intrinsically two-dimensional fixed-point theory compatible with Hilbert space positivity, and what are its central charge and gravitational dressing?

destinations.title: Can curvature-dependent graviton fluctuation couplings support an asymptotically safe UV fixed point, and what backgrounds solve the background and quantum equations of motion, with and without Standard Model matter?

Review how interacting renormalization-group fixed points can provide predictive ultraviolet completions for matter and gravity, and whether gravity–matter interactions could connect Planck-scale dynamics to observable particle physics.

Can demanding ultraviolet-complete gauge and Yukawa sectors constrain unimodular asymptotic safety, standard asymptotically safe gravity, and Weyl-squared gravity? Are the leading Weyl-squared gravitational contributions universal within the functional RG calculation?

What evidence supports asymptotically safe quantum gravity when dynamical metric fluctuations are distinguished from the background, and how are background independence, locality, matter stability and unitarity addressed?
Can global Z_n interactions exist at an asymptotically safe gravity–matter fixed point, emerge as relevant deformations of a U(1)-symmetric fixed point, or generate large scalar mass hierarchies?

Can gravity coupled only to scalar fields admit an asymptotically safe fixed point once unavoidable derivative interactions are included, and can adding fermions or vectors restore viable fixed-point candidates?

Can a direct Lorentzian functional renormalisation group calculation produce an asymptotically safe gravitational fixed point and a graviton spectral function, providing timelike propagators needed for future scattering and unitarity tests?

What evidence, phenomenological predictions, consistency constraints, and unresolved problems characterize asymptotically safe gravity–matter systems, particularly Standard Model and beyond-Standard-Model sectors, as reviewed in January 2022?

How can momentum-dependent form factors in the quantum effective action encode asymptotically safe gravitational observables, connect first-principles calculations to scattering amplitudes, and expose low-energy consistency conditions?

Which matter content and interactions admit an asymptotically safe gravity–matter theory, and can ultraviolet quantum scale symmetry yield testable relations among low-energy Standard Model and beyond-Standard-Model parameters?

Can shift-symmetric kinetic-braiding Horndeski models admit an asymptotically safe quantum-field-theoretic UV completion, and can the resulting coupling constraints remain compatible with dynamical dark energy? A second analysis asks whether a gravitational EFT can yield viable couplings without new strongly coupled subplanckian physics.

Can metric quantum gravity possess an interacting UV fixed point with finitely many relevant directions, connect to general relativity and the Standard Model, and admit acceptable Lorentzian spectral properties? This contribution reviews the fluctuation-based functional RG evidence.

Does asymptotically safe gravity permit a dimension-five scalar ULDM–gauge interaction, and can perturbative gravitational fluctuations generate or enhance that interaction? Projected nuclear-clock sensitivity motivates studying these questions at Planck-suppressed coupling strengths.

Which cosmologically motivated vector–tensor EFTs admit an asymptotically safe quantum-field-theory completion, and how could their UV critical surfaces restrict the infrared parameters relevant to late-time cosmology?

What is the full momentum dependence of the scalar-scalar-graviton vertex within an analytically tractable asymptotic-safety approximation, and does its on-shell limit reproduce gravitational soft divergences? The vertex is an ingredient toward testing unitarity and causality through scattering amplitudes.

destination.title: Computing Calabi–Yau geometry and compactification data
destination.question: How can geometric, numerical and analytic methods determine Calabi–Yau geometry and its compactification consequences?
destination.summary: Internal Ricci-flat metrics form a well-supported core. Period geometry, effective kinetic terms, spectra, normalized interactions, landscape searches and moduli phenomenology provide distinct connected directions. Shared vocabulary does not establish identical targets, regimes or questions.

systems: Calabi–Yau manifolds, with dimensions and construction classes retained by source
Heterotic, orientifold, M-theory and F-theory settings where explicitly supplied
targets: Internal metrics and their moduli dependence
Periods, effective kinetic geometry and perturbative corrections
Spectra, geometric observables and normalized matter interactions
Construction databases, model searches, stabilization and axion inference
regimes: Source-specific classical, perturbative, asymptotic and sampled numerical regimes
assumptions: Numerical membership is retrieval provenance, not scientific equivalence
Approximation accuracy and physical control must be assessed for the intended observable
conventions: An internal Kähler potential, a moduli-space Kähler potential and a matter kinetic metric are different objects
Complex dimension, spacetime dimension and approximation degree remain distinct
Ordinary and pre-Swampland work is eligible without a Swampland interpretation
includes: Analytic and conventional numerical work as well as machine learning
Applications and research roadmaps with their completion status preserved
excludes: Generic language design as a direct compactification result
Formal realizability as an established Calabi–Yau metric problem
Torsional existence, small-cycle control or scalable training inferred solely from a small loss

sources.title: Heterotic String Compactifications on Half-flat Manifolds. II.

evidence.text: How are Kähler and complex-structure deformations represented in the appendix's Calabi–Yau geometry? The setting supplies complex moduli, a holomorphic three-form, and an internal metric for the identities that follow.

sources.title: General Analysis of LARGE Volume Scenarios with String Loop Moduli Stabilisation

evidence.text: Which Calabi–Yau geometries admit nonsupersymmetric AdS minima at exponentially large volume, and when can string loops qualitatively complete Kähler-modulus stabilisation rather than merely perturb an existing minimum?

sources.title: The Leading Quantum Corrections to Stringy Kahler Potentials

evidence.text: What is the leading perturbative α′ correction to Kähler-modulus kinetic terms in heterotic Calabi–Yau compactifications with non-standard embedding, and when does it break four-dimensional no-scale structure?

sources.title: Towards the one-loop Kähler metric of Calabi-Yau orientifolds

evidence.text: What direct one-loop correction do N=1 sectors generate for a closed-string Kähler modulus kinetic term in toroidal Calabi–Yau orientifolds, where massive string states contribute? What additional information is needed to obtain the complete Einstein-frame metric?

sources.title: Heavy Tails in Calabi-Yau Moduli Spaces

evidence.text: Can classical Calabi–Yau Kähler geometry be represented by statistically independent derivatives of K, and how do geometric correlations change metric spectra, curvature contributions to scalar masses, metastability expectations, and axion decay constants?

sources.title: One-modulus Calabi-Yau fourfold reductions with higher-derivative terms

evidence.text: What corrections to the three-dimensional Kähler potential, complex coordinate and no-scale condition follow from reducing available eleven-dimensional eight-derivative terms on a one-Kähler-modulus Calabi–Yau fourfold, and how robust are they against additional G²R³ couplings?

sources.title: Moduli stabilization in asymptotic flux compactifications

evidence.text: How can the operators needed for the sl(2) approximation be obtained from the bigraded components of δ in the Calabi-Yau fourfold case? The source supplies ζ for use in the paper and η as a companion result.

sources.title: Numerical metrics for complete intersection and Kreuzer–Skarke Calabi–Yau manifolds

evidence.text: How can neural networks approximate Ricci-flat metrics on CICY and Kreuzer–Skarke Calabi–Yau manifolds at prescribed complex-structure and Kähler moduli, with numerical integration accurate enough for volumes, slopes and line-bundle HYM connections?

sources.title: On string one-loop correction to the Einstein-Hilbert term and its implications on the Kähler potential

evidence.text: How can the string one-loop Einstein–Hilbert correction be expressed for Calabi–Yau orientifolds, and how large is its contribution to the Einstein-frame Kähler metric near small-cycle limits?

sources.title: cymyc: Calabi-Yau Metrics, Yukawas, and Curvature

evidence.text: How can globally defined numerical tensor fields on Calabi–Yau manifolds supply Ricci-flat metrics, harmonic matter representatives, canonically normalized Yukawa couplings, and moduli-dependent curvature data?

sources.title: Bayesian inference on Calabi-Yau moduli spaces and the axiverse: Experimental data meets string theory

evidence.text: Can Bayesian sampling of Calabi–Yau Kähler moduli space produce theory-informed axion priors and infer geometric or topological information from hypothetical haloscope detections and cosmological likelihoods?

sources.title: What to do with a Ricci-flat Calabi--Yau metric?

evidence.text: What physics and mathematics become computationally accessible once numerical Ricci-flat Calabi–Yau metrics, and eventually bundle data, are available? The focus is a research roadmap for normalized observables and metric geometry rather than developing metric-learning algorithms.

sources.title: Numerical Ricci-flat metrics on K3

evidence.text: Can Ricci-flat Calabi–Yau metrics be computed numerically at prescribed complex-structure and Kähler parameters, and can those metrics yield reliable geometric and spectral observables?

sources.title: Kahler potentials of chiral matter fields for Calabi-Yau string compactifications

evidence.text: Can the leading Kähler-modulus dependence of chiral bifundamental matter metrics be extracted from locality and physical Yukawa scaling, without an explicit string-amplitude calculation on a generic Calabi–Yau?

sources.title: Heterotic String Compactifications on Half-flat Manifolds. II.

evidence.text: Contract each harmonic χ_a with conjugate Ω, multiply by 1/(2||Ω||²), and integrate the pairing of the resulting η representatives. Precise component placements require the original equation or earlier conventions.

sources.title: General Analysis of LARGE Volume Scenarios with String Loop Moduli Stabilisation

evidence.text: Expand the F-term potential in the large-volume limit and classify inverse Kähler-metric scalings. Homogeneity and intersection data connect K^{jj}∼𝒱√τj to isolated local blow-ups and K^{11}∼τ₁² to K3-fibre behaviour.

sources.title: The Leading Quantum Corrections to Stringy Kahler Potentials

evidence.text: Dimensionally reduce the supersymmetry-fixed ten-dimensional action on the α′-corrected background through O(α′²), retaining two spacetime derivatives. Work initially in string frame, then perform a Weyl transformation and dualize the spacetime B field to obtain the Einstein-frame action.

sources.title: Towards the one-loop Kähler metric of Calabi-Yau orientifolds

evidence.text: Construct Kähler-adapted vertex operators by varying the worldsheet action with respect to spacetime moduli, then extract the order-p² term of their two-point function. Supersymmetry removes the purely bosonic contraction; four- and eight-fermion pieces remain, evaluated using theta-function spin-structure identities.

sources.title: Heavy Tails in Calabi-Yau Moduli Spaces

evidence.text: Compute Kähler derivatives through the chain rule using A=∂t/∂τ, obtained by numerically inverting A^{-1}=κt. Algebraic differentiation of the inverse avoids numerical differentiation. Sample positive cone-generator coefficients uniformly, and logarithmically for part of the dataset, with a finite cutoff.

sources.title: One-modulus Calabi-Yau fourfold reductions with higher-derivative terms

evidence.text: Construct a 17-term relevant G²R³ basis using contraction restrictions and the first Bianchi identity; constrain coefficients through lower-dimensional supersymmetry and duality. The explicit five-dimensional constraints are not supplied: the authors instead use the Type IIA constraints.

sources.title: Lectures on Numerical and Machine Learning Methods for Approximating Ricci-flat Calabi-Yau Metrics

evidence.text: How can conventional numerical algorithms and neural networks approximate Ricci-flat metrics on compact Calabi–Yau manifolds, with sufficient accuracy and moduli dependence for string compactification applications?

sources.title: Exact Computation of the Special Geometry for Calabi–Yau Hypersurfaces of Fermat Type

evidence.text: Can the special Kähler potential be computed explicitly for all polynomial complex-structure deformations of Fermat Calabi–Yau hypersurfaces, including the real structure needed to pair their periods?

sources.title: Numerical spectra of the Laplacian for line bundles on Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces

evidence.text: How can one numerically compute eigenvalues and eigenmodes of bundle-valued Dolbeault Laplacians, especially harmonic (0,1)-forms needed to normalize matter fields and physical Yukawa couplings in heterotic compactifications?

sources.title: Calabi–Yau metrics with Kähler moduli dependence

evidence.text: Can numerical Ricci-flat Calabi–Yau metrics be converted into compact analytic approximations with explicit continuous Kähler-moduli dependence, enabling systematic study of metric-dependent quantities across moduli space?

sources.title: Calabi-Yau Spaces in the String Landscape

evidence.text: How do Calabi–Yau compactification geometries arise in string phenomenology, how have explicit construction databases developed, and how can computational geometry and machine learning help explore them? The article concentrates on the Calabi–Yau landscape rather than vacuum-selection probabilities.

sources.title: Moduli-dependent Calabi-Yau and SU(3)-structure metrics from Machine Learning

evidence.text: Can metric learning discover realizable torsional geometries, avoid small cycles, and scale to larger moduli spaces? These remain proposed research directions.

sources.title: Modular forms and hierarchical Yukawa couplings in heterotic Calabi-Yau compactifications

evidence.text: When do instanton-corrected holomorphic Yukawa couplings in heterotic Calabi–Yau compactifications become modular forms, and how do those forms and matter kinetic metrics generate physical Yukawa hierarchies?

sources.title: Moduli-dependent Calabi-Yau and SU(3)-structure metrics from Machine Learning

evidence.text: How can explicit Calabi–Yau metrics be approximated while retaining complex-structure dependence? The appendices distinguish the modulus ψ, which changes the geometry, from the section degree k, which controls the algebraic approximation at fixed geometry.

sources.title: String Model Building, Reinforcement Learning and Genetic Algorithms

evidence.text: Can reinforcement learning and genetic algorithms efficiently locate rare phenomenologically attractive heterotic monad models in spaces too large for systematic scans, and how complete are their searches on the chosen Calabi–Yau examples?

sources.title: Asymptotic String Compactifications: Periods, flux potentials, and the swampland

evidence.text: How can asymptotic Hodge theory organize Calabi–Yau periods and physical couplings near degenerations, enabling calculations of weak-gravity bounds and flux-moduli stabilization beyond large complex structure?

sources.title: Deep-Learning the Landscape

evidence.text: Can neural networks trained on existing mathematical-physics databases rapidly estimate geometric and phenomenological quantities for configurations whose exact computation is expensive, and reveal useful patterns in partial classifications?

sources.title: Evolving neural networks with genetic algorithms to study the String Landscape

evidence.text: Can genetic algorithms select neural-network architectures for string-landscape classification, implementation of known but cumbersome computations, and regression approximations to expensive mathematical calculations?

sources.title: Moduli-dependent KK towers and the swampland distance conjecture on the quintic Calabi-Yau manifold

evidence.text: How do shape changes at fixed internal volume alter scalar KK masses on a quintic Calabi–Yau threefold?

sources.title: Learning Size and Shape of Calabi-Yau Spaces

evidence.text: Can neural networks efficiently approximate Ricci-flat Calabi–Yau metrics for user-specified shape and size moduli, and can inexpensive Monge–Ampère training substitute for direct curvature optimization?

sources.title: Calabi–Yau metrics, energy functionals and machine learning

evidence.text: Can supervised neural-network learning approximate the Kähler-potential data of Headrick–Nassar optimal numerical Calabi–Yau metrics accurately from a small training sample, with reduced computational time?

sources.title: CYJAX: A package for Calabi-Yau metrics with JAX

evidence.text: How can a modular numerical package efficiently approximate Calabi-Yau metrics across complex-structure moduli, helping address the missing metric information needed for low-energy couplings in string compactifications?

sources.title: Physical Yukawa couplings in heterotic string compactifications

evidence.text: How can physically normalized Yukawa couplings associated with H²,¹ of heterotic Calabi–Yau compactifications be computed efficiently? The paper exploits the standard embedding to replace direct Ricci-flat metric and harmonic-form normalization by a Weil–Petersson calculation, with period and machine-learning benchmarks.

sources.title: Calabi-Yau fourfolds for M theory and F theory compactifications

evidence.text: Which explicit Calabi-Yau fourfold deformation families support M- and F-theory compactifications, and how do their topology, instanton divisors, elliptic degenerations, transitions and quantum cohomology encode effective-theory properties?
